Guidance & outlook: On a sequential basis, that is between Q4 of FY26 to Q1 of FY27, both EBITDA and PBT have risen by 12% and 10% respectively.
Now for the FY27 guidance: Looking ahead, we believe FY27 represents an important inflection point in Ganesh Housing's growth journey.
While the revenue could increase substantially, the PAT could rise by about 10% or could just be maintained only because of the exceptional one -time tax hit in Q1 of FY27, which I just explained.
Growth & demand: Today, with approximately 510 acres of land reserves, a strong execution pipeline, and a healthy balance sheet, we believe the company is exceptionally well-positioned to capitalize on the next phase of Ahmedabad's real estate growth.
280 crores, which is a growth of 130% on a sequential basis and 86% on a year -on-year basis.
Strategic land monetization further give additional capital flexibility and our extensive development pipeline positions as well for future launches.
Margins & costs: The EBITDA and PBT on a Y oY basis are slightly lower.
280 crore sale has been done, then why has the operating margin plummeted from 85%, which is the general one, to only 39%.
And the gross margins or EBITDA has been lower because the cost of the land, as you rightly observed, was higher than what we normally have been having in our books.
Capex & expansion: More importantly, we believe we are entering a phase where years of patient investment in land, infrastructure, and execution capabilities are beginning to translate into tangible business opportunities.

Ahmedabad is steadily evolving into one of India's most attractive real estate destinations, supported by sustained infrastructure investments, improved metro connectivity, rapid urban expansion, the continued development of gift city, and increasing interest from domestic as well as global businesses.
Finally, expanding our development pipeline through selective land acquisitions in high-potential locations.
Balance sheet & cash: We have remained disciplined in capital allocation, selective in project development, and focused on building assets that not only create near-term cash flows but also enhance long- term shareholder value.
As we indicated during a previous interaction with investors, the borrowing undertaking during the last five financial year was primarily in the nature of lease rentals, discounting.
700 crores will be realized in terms of the cash flows itself in this year.
Risks & challenges: We got a compelling offer to sell this land rather than developing it and taking the risk of both construction and sale of this multi- storied building over the next five years.
So, three plus two, that is a risk which is associated with it.
But the time period for execution and sale, that is an associated risk.

Guidance & outlook: At the outset, as you all know, FY 26 had been a little problematic year with the West Asia crisis and the economic and geopolitical challenges, which has been reflected in our numbers also when compared to FY 25.
For Q4 FY 26, the company reported revenues of INR122 crores, registering a sequential growth of 33%.
For the full year FY 26, revenue stood at INR539 crores and PAT at INR316 crores.
Growth & demand: Over the last 5 months, the real estate market in Ahmedabad and wider Gujarat has seen a strong mix of infrastructure -led growth, premium housing demand, institutional interest and some emerging cost pressures, of course.
This is due to better road infrastructure, industrial growth, warehousing and logistics demand, data centers and fintech ecosystem and township developments.

And these companies continue to launch projects and they are able to successfully do that, take the market, gai n market share, while Ganesh continues to not launch and hence, thereby lose market share.
Margins & costs: EBITDA stood at INR98 crores with EBITDA margins of about 80.7% and PAT came in at INR 61 crores with PAT margins of about 50%.

So One 91 Thaltej has a sale value of INR 2,100 crores and the cost of about -- so include land cost is about INR1,500.
Capex & expansion: The biggest driver con tinues to be the combined impact of GIFT City, metro expansion and large-scale urban development.
The operationalization and expansion of Phase 2 of Gujarat Metro Rail Corporation, metro network have become a major valuation trigger.
Motera and SG Highway especially are seeing stronger investment interest.
Balance sheet & cash: We are pleased to state that looking to the strong cash flows that the company has, the Board of Directors have recommended a dividend of 15%, that is INR1.5 per share.

My last question is that like our dividend payout, though we declared a 15% dividend, in 2024, it was 110% dividend, which came down to 50% and it is right now 15%.
Risks & challenges: Due to this uncertainty, the cost of input materials and many other things have gone up, as you all know.
Of course, there are certain emerging challenges of increased construction costs and project delays, but these are either manageable or surmountable.
And then when that next quarter comes, that is further delayed by a quarter.
